beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:reverent, setting the scene]A wooden ^chest, covered in ^gold, about the size of a large travel ^trunk. [act:simple, a detail][tune:level]Carried on two ^poles. [act:wonder, slower]The Ark of the Covenant: the most famous ^lost object@noun on Earth.
[d:tension][act:respectful, measured]Yet a church in Ethiopia holds that it was ^never lost. [act:curious, gently][tune:rise]Can that be ^tested?

[d:calm][act:grounded, interested]Start with the ^description, in the book of Exodus. [act:explaining, clear]It fits its ^world: gilded shrines carried on poles are well known from ^Egypt. [go:4|0][act:quieter, the mystery begins]Then the chest ^vanishes from the record@noun, around the fall of ^Jerusalem to Babylon, in about {586|five eighty-six} BCE. [p:0.93][act:precise, a telling detail]The Bible lists what the Babylonians carried ^away: bronze pillars, pots and ^shovels. [act:quiet, pointed][tune:fall]The Ark is ^not on the list.

[d:build][act:respectful, hushed]Now travel south, to Aksum, in the highlands of ^Ethiopia. [act:respectful, hushed]There, ^one monk guards a small chapel for ^life. [sfx:shimmer][act:quiet, simple]^Nobody else goes in: not ^pilgrims, not ^scholars, not ^cameras. [act:sincere, with care][tune:fall]The tradition is ^sincere, ^old, and central to a ^living church.

[d:build][go:3|0][act:plain, even, factual]But its ^written form, a book called the Kebra Nagast, comes about nineteen ^hundred years after the Ark leaves the record@noun. [p:0.93][act:explaining, an image]Nineteen centuries: as long as from the Roman Empire to ^today.

[d:build][act:fair, recounting it]The writer Graham Hancock traced a ^route: from ^Jerusalem, to a Jewish temple on the ^Nile, to an island in Lake ^Tana, and on to ^Aksum. [d:aside][act:even, generous][tune:fallrise]^Real places, all of them. [act:plain, careful]But ^no source says the Ark passed ^through them. [act:explaining, fair]A line drawn between real dots is still only a ^line.

[d:reveal][act:storytelling, a hush]Now go back to Jerusalem, in sixty-three BCE. [act:storytelling, vivid]The Roman general Pompey walks into the Temple's ^holiest room, the room where tradition placed the ^Ark. [sfx:hit][act:the reveal, quiet][tune:fall]The historian Tacitus says he found it ^empty. [act:with care, reflective]Whatever the Ark's fate, it had ^already happened.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, respectful][tune:rise]The Ark at ^Aksum? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Awaiting ^evidence*. [act:even, balanced][tune:level]Nothing ^contradicts it. [act:the same weight, calm][tune:fall]Nothing ^supports it. [act:with care, sincere]And the faith of those who keep it is not ours to ^weigh.

[d:tension][p:0.93][act:thoughtful, a quiet wish]^One radiocarbon date, on one sliver of wood, would tell us its ^age. [act:explaining, brief]Wood carries a carbon clock that starts ticking when the tree is ^felled. [gap:0.45][act:the last word, gentle, accepting][tune:fall]But the door stays ^shut.
